criteria.detail: All 8 ACs implemented, including the admin delivery surface.
Current and records the AC-001 timing limitation.
One feature on the shared branch; an admin test mock was extended for the new query.
Retry cap measured against real mutations; hostile escaping payloads; authorisation tested both ways.
Production audit clean; escaped interpolation; one recipient per send; admin-only delivery query.
Test report and plan match the implementation.
NFR-001/002/003/004 tested. AC-001's 60-second delivery window is unverified because no provider is configured in tests; recorded rather than claimed.
Satisfied, with the timing limitation named.

findings.issue: AC-001's 60-second delivery window is unverified; scheduling is proven, delivery timing is not, because no provider is configured in tests.
A stale-delivery bug (dialog rendered while closed, invalid timestamp) was found and fixed during this round.

security.reason: Production dependency audit is clean (0 vulnerabilities with --omit=dev). Template interpolation is escaped, each send has exactly one recipient, the delivery query is admin-only and tested from both sides, and the preference mutation only patches the caller's own registrations.

baseline.detail: setEmailPreference patches only the caller's registrations; getRegistrationEmailDeliveries requires admin.
All new functions take validated args.
Every interpolated value is escaped before it reaches the HTML body.
Provider credentials remain in environment variables.

performance.reason: The confirmation is scheduled rather than awaited, so provider latency never reaches the registration mutation; sweeps are bounded to 100 items per run and read through an index; no bundle growth.
performance.method: Code review of the dispatch path plus the sweep bounds.

nfr.target: confirmation transactional, optional email honours the preference
registration latency independent of the provider
